title: Can You Spot the AI?
summary: Students write two persuasive essays on the same topic, one independently and one with GenAI, and submit them anonymously for peer detection. They then analyze peers' guesses and reflect on AI writing, detection limits, ethical use, and their original prediction.

sources.title: Can You Spot the AI? Incorporating GenAI into Technical Writing Assignments
sources.evidence_quote: Students are tasked with writing two persuasive essays, one without the use of genAI and the other with the assistance of a genAI tool.

context.discipline: technical writing, professional responsibility, and ethics

assessment.summary: Produce matched human- and AI-assisted essays, detect AI assistance in peers' work, and reflect on the results.
student_actions: Write a persuasive essay without GenAI.
Write a second essay with GenAI assistance.
Predict whether peers will identify the AI-assisted essay.
Review two peers' essay pairs and justify detection decisions.
Compare the prediction with peer guesses.

structure.name: Peer Review
structure.description: Identify AI-assisted peer essays and explain the decision.

structure.name: Did They Spot the AI?
structure.description: Reflect on detection results and GenAI.

student_role.description: GenAI is required for one essay and prohibited for the matched student-only essay.

prohibited_actions: Using GenAI to write the student-only essay

grading.method: Students are graded primarily on ethical GenAI use and critical reflection rather than writing quality.

reported_results: Student feedback indicated that the activity was engaging and improved understanding of GenAI limitations and use cases.
